findings.text: the new sentence infers from the absence of `section_readiness` that "no section of the plan is blocked", but `build_roadmap` attaches it only when `section_dependency_blockers or mapped_edges or decision_section_blockers` holds (`reckon/roadmap.py:3578`), while an own-plan section gate is held through `split_unpassed_gates`'s second return and recorded only in `section_holds_by_plan` (`reckon/roadmap.py:3650-3652`); demonstrated on the tree: `split_unpassed_gates({'section_declarations':{'s1':'implementable','s2':'implementable'},'gates':[{'id':'g1','status':'open','gated_sections':['s1']}]})` returns `plan_holding=[]`, `section_gate=[('g1',['s1'])]`, so a plan whose only hold is that gate gets no `section_readiness`, and a waiter that reads absence as ready launches the dependent section before `g1` passes
